what_happened: The operator ran the CI routing build (job d5gk) directly, ahead of its place in Athena's plan, where it was 12th. The operator's reason was that parallel runs and big jobs kept hitting deadlines because builds were cold and local. CI routing was the work that would fix that. This is the fourth time the operator has overridden the plan's order for the owner's speed work.
cause: The plan does not use the owner's stated priority, or the live failure pressure, to decide order. Rungs are sequenced by default type and position. Nothing compares the plan's order with the owner's latest priority. Nothing moves a job up when it would remove a recurring failure such as deadline hits, and the queue has no priority support. The only way to change order is for the operator to bypass the plan. Earlier gaps about this were logged but never turned into a fix, so the bypass keeps recurring.
prevention: Make owner priority an input to planning and to the queue. Let an addendum or operator mark a rung with a priority. Have the planner sort by that priority ahead of default rung order. Add a check that fails plan generation when the top stated priority has work ranked below lower-priority rungs. Add queue priority support so a reordered item runs next without the operator running it by hand. Where a job would remove a recurring cause of failures, such as cold local builds causing deadline hits, the planner should be able to raise it from that evidence.
proposed_request: Make Athena's plan and queue respect the owner's stated priority. Outcome: when the owner's latest addendum or the operator names a priority, such as speed, or a job that removes a recurring failure, the plan puts the matching rungs ahead of default-ordered rungs, and the queue runs them first without the operator running them directly. Plan generation must fail with a clear message if the top stated priority has work ranked below lower-priority work. Acceptance: (1) a test with an addendum naming speed as top priority shows speed rungs, including the CI routing build, ordered first; (2) a queue item with higher priority is drained before older lower-priority items; (3) a plan whose order contradicts the latest stated priority is rejected by a code check, not only by prompt wording; (4) the existing gap k0w6 is closed by this work.
